public_rationale: No decisive counterexample meeting the stated rule was established. The Sierra Leone study finds AI access cheaper than loading webpages, but includes users' mobile-data charges and AI API prices. Treating that as a measurement of providers' serving costs would change the comparison. The forecast therefore remains open; elapsed time without a qualifying counterexample does not prove always.
limitations: A broader user-price reading would make the study substantially more adverse to the claim.
Unspecified workloads and cost allocation limit comparisons.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Processing a generative AI request will always cost more than serving a webpage.

statement.excerpt: Moreover, the scale is different, and serving a webpage will always cost less than processing a request sent to a generative AI model.

from_speaker: processing a request sent to a generative AI model
our_interpretation: The surrounding discussion concerns infrastructure providers and application operators. The ordinary reading compares their serving costs, not users' mobile-data charges.
Always asserts a permanent cost ordering, not merely a typical difference in February 2024.
A fair comparison must specify the webpage, model request, utilization and cost boundary. Neither free promotional pricing nor an unusually wasteful webpage is sufficient by itself.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable measurements may support the ordering for measured workloads and dates, but finite observations cannot establish that it will always hold.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A reproducible comparison demonstrates a genuine generative-model request costing no more to serve than an ordinary webpage under a consistent provider-side cost boundary.

evidence.explanation: The study compares mobile-data charges for loading webpages with AI token prices plus mobile-data charges. It challenges a user-cost reading, but does not measure both providers' underlying serving expenses.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A dated, reproducible comparison showing generative inference at or below ordinary webpage-serving cost under a consistent provider-side cost boundary would contradict the claim.
